name: Tree-Ring Crossdating
mechanism: Match overlapping sequences of ring-width patterns to establish a supported relative or anchored calendar chronology.
operating_requirement: Attributable wood samples, prepared surfaces, magnification, measured ring series, overlapping reference samples and analyst time.
consequence: Dates qualified growth sequences; absent outer rings do not establish a felling date, and an unanchored sequence remains floating.
semantic_boundary: Seasonal observation recognizes recurrence; crossdating resolves correspondence between retained annual sequences. A climate interpretation still requires proxy calibration.
implementation_acceptance: Introduce a missing or false ring and require inconsistent matches to be flagged; no calendar year appears without an anchored reference.
branching_note: All named foundations apply. Instruments, samples and reference services remain separate paid physical requirements; knowledge does not create equipment or evidence.
recovery: Acquire attributable method instruction, samples or specialist service through a reachable competent partner, then fund a local qualification.

name: Varve Chronology Correlation
mechanism: Correlate qualified annual sediment couplets across overlapping cores while retaining counting gaps and ambiguous layers.
operating_requirement: Actual undisturbed cores, section preparation, optical measurements, independent annuality evidence and finite correlation work.
consequence: Constrains elapsed sediment accumulation time; erosion, disturbances and unverified annuality prevent an exact continuous calendar.
semantic_boundary: Core reconstruction preserves sequences; this specifically tests annual layer correspondence and accumulated counting uncertainty.
implementation_acceptance: A missing core interval remains a gap; a storm layer cannot be counted as a year solely because it is visible.

name: Radiocarbon Calendar Calibration
mechanism: Map a measured conventional radiocarbon age and its uncertainty through an attributable calibration curve and an appropriate reservoir model.
operating_requirement: Prepared dated sample, actual qualified carbon measurement, blanks and standards, applicable curve version, sample-context evidence and analysis work.
consequence: Produces a possibly disjoint calendar-age range; contamination or unsupported reservoir correction prevents a confident event date.
semantic_boundary: General isotope geochronology does not equate conventional radiocarbon years to calendar years. A sample date is not automatically the age of its surrounding artifact or water body.
implementation_acceptance: Retain separate probability ranges where the curve permits multiple dates; changing reservoir evidence must change or invalidate the result.

name: Luminescence Sediment Dating
mechanism: Combine an observed trapped-charge luminescence dose with a qualified environmental dose rate to estimate time since a supported resetting event.
operating_requirement: Light-protected suitable mineral sample, preparation, controlled stimulation and photon detection, dose references, environmental and moisture evidence, instrument time.
consequence: Constrains burial or resetting age; incomplete bleaching, unstable signal or unsupported dose history prevents an unconditional age.
semantic_boundary: Measures accumulated trapped charge rather than a parent/daughter isotope ratio. Sample exposure during collection can destroy the relevant record.
implementation_acceptance: A light-exposed or incompletely reset sample must not yield the same accepted burial date as a qualified specimen; dose-rate uncertainty propagates.

name: Cosmogenic Surface Exposure Dating
mechanism: Interpret measured in-situ cosmogenic nuclide concentration using a qualified production and surface-history model.
operating_requirement: Located rock specimens, separation chemistry, sensitive isotope analysis, production-rate references, shielding and erosion evidence, field and laboratory labor.
consequence: Constrains surface residence or erosion; inherited nuclides and changing cover can prevent a unique exposure age.
semantic_boundary: Near-surface production is part of this clock, unlike a generic closed decay system; it does not directly date initial rock crystallization.
implementation_acceptance: Changing documented cover or inherited concentration changes the inferred interval; the method cannot reveal an unvisited surface.
branching_note: All named foundations apply. Instruments, samples and reference services remain separate paid physical requirements; knowledge does not create equipment or evidence.

name: Paired-Nuclide Burial Histories
mechanism: Use two measured cosmogenic nuclides with different decay behavior to constrain exposure followed by burial under an explicit history model.
operating_requirement: A qualified common specimen, both isotope measurements, correlated uncertainties, production and burial-shielding assumptions, finite model comparison.
consequence: Can distinguish some burial histories that a single concentration cannot resolve; complex re-exposure can remain ambiguous.
semantic_boundary: Adds a two-nuclide history constraint, not another name for a single surface-exposure clock.
implementation_acceptance: Withhold a unique burial duration when two incompatible histories fit the observations; one isotope alone cannot satisfy the method.
branching_note: All named foundations apply. Instruments, samples and reference services remain separate paid physical requirements; knowledge does not create equipment or evidence.

name: Fission-Track Thermochronology
mechanism: Compare retained fission-track counts and length distributions with qualified annealing behavior to constrain a mineral thermal history.
operating_requirement: Prepared suitable grains, track microscopy and calibration, mineral-composition evidence, an applicable annealing model and paid interpretation.
consequence: Constrains a range of cooling or heating histories; mineral chemistry and model extrapolation uncertainty remain visible.
semantic_boundary: Track damage and its thermal shortening are the observations; a track age alone is not a universal crystallization date or exact peak temperature.
implementation_acceptance: Different track-length distributions at similar apparent ages must affect the allowed history; unsupported annealing calibration prevents a precise reconstruction.

name: Argon Step-Heating Interpretation
mechanism: Interpret a measured incremental argon-release age spectrum and associated uncertainties to assess a supported geological age component.
operating_requirement: Suitable prepared mineral, qualified irradiation service and reference monitors, maintained vacuum extraction and heating, isotope measurements, blanks and analyst work.
consequence: Disturbed steps or excess argon can defeat a plateau interpretation; a reported age retains the selected steps and released-gas fraction.
semantic_boundary: A sequence of measured release fractions tests internal consistency beyond a bulk isotope age. It provides no automatic cooling or crystallization label.
implementation_acceptance: Discordant release steps cannot be silently averaged into a precise plateau; missing reference or blank evidence blocks qualification.
